newsitem.title: POLAND: BIG agrees to up Gdanski stake.
newsitem.headline: BIG agrees to up Gdanski stake.

text.p: Polish bank BIG SA has agreed with the state treasury to raise its stake in Bank Gdanski SA by 6,260,240 shares, or 31.9 percent, to about 63 percent at 40 zlotys per share, BIG said in a statement on Friday.
BIG, which holds its Gdanski shares directly and through two subsidiaries, was the only bidder for the treasury's offer of the stake in Gdanski.

Earlier this month BIG, whose full name is Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych SA, received the permission of the National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank, to hold between 50 and 66 percent of Gdanski.
Gdanski closed on the bourse on Friday at 47 zlotys.
The Bank of New York as a depositary bank currently holds 19.5 percent of Gdanski's shares, represented by the bank's GDRs held by foreign investors.
The treasury plans to hold on to about five percent of Gdanski shares.
Small investors on the Warsaw bourse hold the remaining shares.
